subject.title: Unhandled Playwright assertion error in CRSession._onMessage crashes Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw handle these Playwright CDP assertion escapes with a narrow browser-owned quarantine/reconnect boundary, or make browser/CDP control a larger subprocess/external-service isolation project?
rationale: Current source proves the fatal path is still plausible, but the safe fix shape is a product/runtime boundary decision because blanket process-level suppression could hide serious browser protocol failures.

options.title: Narrow browser-owned quarantine
options.body: Reproduce the CRSession/CRBrowser assertion live, then handle only confirmed Playwright CDP assertion escapes by disconnecting/quarantining that browser profile and returning browser errors while preserving the fatal policy for unknown process-level rejections.

options.title: Subprocess isolation project
options.body: Treat this as a larger architecture effort to move browser/CDP control out of the main Gateway process, using this issue as the design tracker rather than a small repair candidate.

options.title: Document external workaround only
options.body: Keep raw CDP as-is and steer affected users toward Chrome MCP or external bridge patterns, accepting that some raw CDP assertion escapes can still restart Gateway.

recommendation.title: Narrow browser-owned quarantine
recommendation.body: Reproduce the CRSession/CRBrowser assertion live, then handle only confirmed Playwright CDP assertion escapes by disconnecting/quarantining that browser profile and returning browser errors while preserving the fatal policy for unknown process-level rejections.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across both the browser/CDP path and global unhandled-rejection policy.
